product_brief: IOTA Identity library for issuing and verifying Verifiable Credentials and Presentations, with v1.7 adding post-quantum signature support.
pqc_support: Yes — v1.7 supports ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, and FALCON signatures for JWT-based VCs/VPs, plus hybrid (ML-DSA + Ed25519) composite keys
pqc_capability_description: IOTA Identity v1.7 can issue and verify JWT-based VCs and VPs signed with ML-DSA (levels 44, 65, 87), SLH-DSA (128/192/256), and FALCON (512/1024), with PQ keys as JWK (kty "AKP"). Hybrid compositeJwk supports id-MLDSA44-Ed25519 and id-MLDSA65-Ed25519. Usable only if the key storage supports them.
crypto_primitives: RSA, EdDSA, ECDSA (traditional, noted as quantum-vulnerable); Ed25519; ML-DSA; SLH-DSA; FALCON
key_management_model: Pluggable key storage (Storage/key store); PQC use depends on key storage support (e.g., in-memory JwkPqMemStore in examples)
supported_blockchains: IOTA (DID method did:iota); also ephemeral DIDs did:jwk, did:key, did:compositejwk
architecture_type: Library/SDK (Rust and WASM/TypeScript bindings) for DID and Verifiable Credential operations
signature_schemes: RSA, EdDSA, ECDSA, Ed25519 (traditional); ML-DSA-44/65/87, SLH-DSA, FALCON-512/1024; hybrid id-MLDSA44-Ed25519 and id-MLDSA65-Ed25519
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Hybrid signatures enable a smooth, phased migration to PQC; PQ VC workflow is similar to traditional, though keys, verifiers, and signature sizes differ (e.g., 4627-byte ML-DSA-87 signature, 2592-byte public key). A non-PQC DLT storing the DID Document remains unsafe.

evidence.PQC Support: The release of IOTA Identity v1.7 introduces support for post-quantum cryptography techniques.
evidence.PQC Capability Description: IOTA Identity can verify JWT-based VCs and VPs that are signed using various PQC algorithms, as well as handling PQC cryptomaterial in JWK format.
evidence.Latest Version: The release of IOTA Identity v1.7 introduces support for post-quantum cryptography techniques.
evidence.Crypto Primitives: The cryptographic algorithms currently used for these signatures - e.g. RSA, EdDSA, ECDSA - are vulnerable to quantum attacks.
evidence.Signature Schemes: The currently supported algorithms for compositeJwk are: id-MLDSA44-Ed25519 and id-MLDSA65-Ed25519 .
